pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**

/kind fix
/sig apps 

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Supports DaemonSets in disruption controller by adding /scale subresource to daemonsets API. It allows to control the eviction rate of DaemonSet pods. 

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

#108124 

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:

```release-note
Added /scale  subresource to DaemonSet API to support of PodDisruptionBudget for DaemonSet pods.
```

This should probably have a KEP. https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/963 is the KEP for adding support for the scale subresource in PDBs

@mortent @smarterclayton Thank you for your feedback. There is no KEP for this by now,  I'll add one. And I'll look into implementing the scale subresource for DS.

> How will this interact with the eviction api, in particular the kubectl drain command that has a --ignore-daemonsets flag?

PDB's `status.disruptionsAllowed` calculates correctly that leads to the desired eviction behavior.

The `--ignore-daemonsets` flag on draining leaves DS pods untouched, and PDB's 'status.disruptionsAllowed' does not change. From the perspective of DS pods and its PDB, nothing changes.

I have a drain patch that went rotten for draining daemonsets here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/88345

I can revive if necessary if we decide to support this DaemonSet option in PDBs.  Right now, 'drain' is really the only (I might be making this up) client that supports the eviction API, so we'd want to get in my change or a similar one.

@liggitt @shvgn @mortent 

I have tested the eviction API on this feature branch. I had 3 nodes.
```
NAME          READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE     IP              NODE            NOMINATED NODE   READINESS GATES
nginx-g6pvd   1/1     Running   0          3m35s   172.16.87.193   worker-node01   <none>           <none>
nginx-rpspl   1/1     Running   0          3m35s   172.16.77.129   master-node     <none>           <none>
nginx-wzpl6   0/1     Running   0          3m35s   172.16.158.1    worker-node02   <none>           <none>
```

My PDB was:
```
spec:
  unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy: IfHealthyBudget
  maxUnavailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nginx
```

As you see I had one `Unready` pod.

Drain didn't work  without `--ignore-daemonsets`.
```
kubectl drain worker-node02
node/worker-node02 cordoned
error: unable to drain node "worker-node02" due to error:cannot delete DaemonSet-managed Pods (use --ignore-daemonsets to ignore): default/nginx-wzpl6, kube-system/calico-node-c5ptx, continuing command...
There are pending nodes to be drained:
 worker-node02
cannot delete DaemonSet-managed Pods (use --ignore-daemonsets to ignore): default/nginx-wzpl6, kube-system/calico-node-c5ptx
```

I executed drain command with `--ignore-daemonsets`.
```
kubectl drain worker-node02 --ignore-daemonsets
node/worker-node02 already cordoned
Warning: ignoring DaemonSet-managed Pods: default/nginx-wzpl6, kube-system/calico-node-c5ptx
node/worker-node02 drained
```

The node became `SchedulingDisabled`.
```
NAME            STATUS                     ROLES    AGE   VERSION
master-node     Ready                      <none>   24m   v1.27.0-alpha.0.1223+7e70ab029313a6
worker-node01   Ready                      <none>   23m   v1.27.0-alpha.0.1223+7e70ab029313a6
worker-node02   Ready,SchedulingDisabled   <none>   23m   v1.27.0-alpha.0.1223+7e70ab029313a6
```

As i see it is working as expected, PDB didn't make any effect on eviction API.

Regarding my question:

> Separately, what are the implications of making PDB consider daemonset pods. Does this have the potential to make the /evict API return errors in cases where it is currently working?

It seems like the goal of this PR is to make the eviction API start preventing deletion of daemonset pods (when PDB forbids it) where it previously did not... is that correct?

> PDB didn't make any effect on eviction API.

I'm having a hard time understanding how that is the case... I thought the point of this PR was to make it have an effect

@liggitt @shvgn @mortent

> I'm having a hard time understanding how that is the case... I thought the point of this PR was to make it have an effect

I can't speak about others use cases, but we would like to use PDB during Kubernetes upgrade, where `drain`-ing the node isn't necessary (fixme). What we would like to achieve is to control how many nodes should be down at a time during the upgrade. 

What I have proved here is the change didn't affect the functionality of the drain.

On the other hand, there is a significant difference when we are calling eviction endpoint:
```bash
kubectl get po
NAME          READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
nginx-459sp   0/1     Running   0          33s
nginx-8sv67   1/1     Running   0          60m
nginx-ww82h   1/1     Running   0          60m
```

I couldn't evict a `healthy` pod, because an other is `unhealthy`.
```bash
curl -v -H 'Content-type: application/json' https://192.168.56.10:6443/api/v1/namespaces/default/pods/nginx-8sv67/eviction -d @eviction.json --insecure
{
  "kind": "Status",
  "apiVersion": "v1",
  "metadata": {},
  "status": "Failure",
  "message": "Cannot evict pod as it would violate the pod's disruption budget.",
  "reason": "TooManyRequests",
  "details": {
    "causes": [
      {
        "reason": "DisruptionBudget",
        "message": "The disruption budget nginx needs 2 healthy pods and has 2 currently"
      }
    ]
  },
  "code": 429
```

With default `unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy: IfHealthyBudget` I wasn't able to evict the `unhealthy` pod.
```bash
curl -v -H 'Content-type: application/json' https://192.168.56.10:6443/api/v1/namespaces/default/pods/nginx-459sp/eviction -d @eviction.json --insecure
{
  "kind": "Status",
  "apiVersion": "v1",
  "metadata": {},
  "status": "Failure",
  "message": "Cannot evict pod as it would violate the pod's disruption budget.",
  "reason": "TooManyRequests",
  "details": {
    "causes": [
      {
        "reason": "DisruptionBudget",
        "message": "The disruption budget nginx is still being processed by the server."
      }
    ],
    "retryAfterSeconds": 10
  },
  "code": 429
```

But after I changed `unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy` to `AlwaysAllow`, I was able to evict the `unhealthy` pod.
```bash
curl -v -H 'Content-type: application/json' https://192.168.56.10:6443/api/v1/namespaces/default/pods/nginx-459sp/eviction -d @eviction.json --insecure
{
  "kind": "Status",
  "apiVersion": "v1",
  "metadata": {},
  "status": "Success",
  "code": 201
```

So as I see:
- this change doesn't break the functionality of `unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy` because daemonset pod just works like any other pod in the system.
- eviction API works well with `maxUnavailable` field on daeonset pods.
- this change doesn't break the functionality of `drain`. Users are still able to drain nodes and leave daemonsets running via `--ignore-daemonsets`.

I don't understand what a scale subresource means for a DaemonSet. What I think it'd mean is that setting scale to `2` means I want two copies on each selected node.

@shvgn, you'd really need a KEP to make this proposal land.

> @sftim, there was a KEP, but after that, we agreed that this is more a bug than a feature, so KEP is not required.

I don't see how absence of a scale subresource for daemonset is a bug... this definitely seems like a feature, and one which (in my opinion) needs more evidence / understanding / design before being accepted or implemented

@liggitt the initial attempt to write a KEP was here https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3089, but [per comment](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3089#issuecomment-1040306353) was closed. Should a new KEP for a scale subresource be introduced? Should we discuss offered solution once more (and probably reconsider it)?

If we want to narrowly make PDB work specifically with daemonset pods and consider it *not* interoperating with daemonset pods a bug, that's one thing.

If we want to fix that issue by adding a scale subresource to DaemonSet, I think that needs a KEP, since it has implications way beyond PDB.

As @sftim mentioned, the whole idea seems odd, like how can we scale pods for the controller that suppose to run pods on every node? However, ignoring PDB is another odd thing because PDB is not about scaling (despite being connected to a scale subresource in other controllers' implementation). 

My intention is only to fix PDB, not invent a whole new conception of daemonset scaling.

so maybe that means teaching the disruption controller about daemonsets specifically in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c18428423a474e517c27c0fc2cfcb110bcec62d2/pkg/controller/disruption/disruption.go#L244-L258 (like it already knows about replicasets, etc, specifically)

> As @sftim mentioned, the whole idea seems odd, like how can we scale pods for the controller that suppose to run pods on every node? However, ignoring PDB is another odd thing because PDB is not about scaling (despite being connected to a scale subresource in other controllers' implementation).

I just want to emphasise, that this is about adding a read only scale subresource, so we would not have to solve scaling of the DS in any sense.

But since adding only part of the scale API could have implications for other users, adding the DS finder seems like a simpler/easier thing to do in the short term.
Hey, @shvgn do you plan to get back to this PR? If not I can take over and go with the `teaching the disruption controller about daemonsets specifically` approach. (I'm working on it)

issue_context.title: Support PDBs for DS
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

While reviewing https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3089 @smarterclayton suggested that PDBs should be opaque to the backing controllers for the pods. As of now, PDBs are not supported for DS since it doesn't have scale subresource. Clayton suggested to introduce a read only scale subresource to DS so that PDBs can be supported for DS. 


In addition, we are going to have an e2e which proves that the PDB can work for any arbitrary controller and minAvailable should work for out of tree controllers. We should make this part of conformance test

### What did you expect to happen?

PDB working for DS just like for deployment or other controllers

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

- Create a PDB
- Map it to DS
- PDB is not honored while evicting pods for DS

### Anything else we need to know?

is this number accurate for using the way PDB is going to use it (to calculate percent available as status.replicas / spec.replicas)? I recall difficulties with the daemonset embedding scheduler logic to determine which nodes to spawn pods for (e.g. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/94722)

Yes, daemon controller has its own scheduling logic but it is consistent for the controller itself.

The issues mentioned was about daemon controller not taking into account all scheduling constraints/options and ignoring particular nodes altogether.


We can see that the controller uses NodeShouldRunDaemonPod to decide which pods to create in 
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5d9d06aa4749ef9ad73f94fef0ef2e56719f9190/pkg/controller/daemon/daemon_controller.go#L782

Then it uses the same logic (NodeShouldRunDaemonPod) to compute the status and desiredNumberScheduled

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5d9d06aa4749ef9ad73f94fef0ef2e56719f9190/pkg/controller/daemon/daemon_controller.go#L1132


So semantically it should be equivalent to the replicas field.

 
We can see that in the same place we are also computing currentNumberScheduled 

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5d9d06aa4749ef9ad73f94fef0ef2e56719f9190/pkg/controller/daemon/daemon_controller.go#L1137 which is equivalent to the number of existing pods.

I think the status fields' names are a bit of misleading since the `Scheduled` part means that it was created/scheduled by the daemon controller and not neceserially recognized by the scheduler yet.
